findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair:

1. The facility got a new double-door standing cooler and the gaskets are observed to be in disrepair. Discussed replacing the gaskets. 
2. There is ice accumulation on the fan unit of the walk-in freezer. Ensure that the issue causing the ice accumulation is repaired and that the ice is removed. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the 
requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of the double door standing cooler to be in disrepair. Inspector showed the equipment to the person in charge (PIC), who stated they will put a work order in. Ensure gaskets are replaced by the next routine inspection so that all equipment is in proper repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed spilled milk at the bottom of the kitchen's reach in milk cooler. Person in charge (PIC) stated that the cooler is cleaned on a weekly basis, but had missed it’s cleaning last week. Continue cleaning schedule and clean spills as they occur.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Daylight is visible along the bottom edge of the back door when shut. Replace the door sweep to protect against the entry of pests.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. [C]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
An unlabeled spray bottle of clear liquid was observed. CORRECTED- PIC identified the bottles contents as bleach and labeled the bottle accordingly. Ensure all containers of chemicals are labeled.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Container of cottage cheese in the walk-in cooler observed with a manufacturer best by date of 1/26/23. CORRECTED- Out of date food was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Mouse droppings were observed on the floor in the corners of the dry storage room and at the west end of the kitchen. Accumulation of general buildup and debris were also observed in the corners at the west end of the kitchen. Detail clean along walls and in corners throughout the kitchen with extra attention given to the corners at the west end of the kitchen and the dry storage room. See general comments for additional information. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Mouse droppings were observed on the floor in the corners of the dry storage room, at the west end of the kitchen, and in the dish room. Accumulation of general buildup and food debris were also observed in the corners at the west end of the kitchen. Manager verified a mouse was caught in the kitchen back in February, but no current rodent activity has been observed. Detail clean along walls and in corners throughout the kitchen, dish room, and dry storage to remove all droppings and general debris (see general comments for additional information).
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed. Ensure use of a barrier to shut off manual faucet of handwashing sink. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Spaghetti sauce was observed with a date mark of 8/30 in the 2 door cooler. Manager stated it was a leftover portion of meatless sauce that was not used. Manager was advised on use or discard of foods within 7 days or less. Sauce was discarded during inspection. Educational handout on date marking was provided (see general comments for additional details).
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometers (0F-220F range) available for use were reading differently at ambient temperature. One thermometer was reading above 60F while the other was reading below 60F. Manager obtained ice for calibration.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to +/-2F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 Can opener had some residue stuck on the edge of the blade. Staff noted the can opener was cleaned after use earlier that morning. Can opener was placed in dish area to go through ware washing again. Staff were advised on precleaning and repeating the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade and was not properly cleaned and sanitized after use the previous operating day. Can opener was placed in dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned and sanitized at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred, between uses, and up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 One of the metal stem food thermometers used at the facility was not accurate. Two thermometers were reading at 68F-70F at room temperature, while the other thermometer was reading closer to 80F. All thermometers were checked with ice water, and the thermometer that was not accurate was calibrated to 32F. The other two thermometers were observed to be at 32F without the need for adjustment. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Internal temperature of one portion of baked beans was observed at 129°F in the warmer; another portion of beans in the same warmer had an internal temperature of 137°F. Internal temperature for meatloaf sandwiches were observed at 114°F and 122°F. Staff noted foods were finished cooking and portioning began around 930a. Final cook temperature for both beans and meatloaf was 150°F. Staff were advised to monitor the temperature of hot foods once they are done cooking and in the process of being portioned. If necessary, place a portion of the product in the warmer and rotate as needed while portioning hot foods to help maintain foods at 135°F/above for hot holding. Lunch starts at 1120a, and all foods would be served or discarded by 1210p. 

Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control hot food that requires time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.
